programs.nl_rule:
a few scattered colored cells on a unicolored background.

there is a unique center of the colored cells, to which each colored cell has a diagonal offset. move diagonally from each colored cell until you are one cell away from the unique center cell. This cell is colored in the color of the starting cell. The unique center cell is colored grey.

The input and output grid have the same shape.

content.text:
Let me understand the rule and the verifier program carefully.

The verifier's transform:
1. Find all colored (nonzero) cells.
2. Find the row `k` with the most colored cells. Take the columns in that row, sorted. a = min col, b = max col. c = (a+b)//2, d = (b-a)//2.
3. Center column c. Center row candidates: r1 = k-d, r2 = k+d. Find the candidate where for every colored cell, |ri - cand_r| == |ci - c|.
4. Set grid[center_r][center_c] = 5 (grey).
5. For each colored cell, dr = ri - center_r, dc = ci - center_c. s_dr, s_dc are signs. If either is 0, skip. add_r = center_r + s_dr, add_c = center_c + s_dc. Set grid[add_r][add_c] = col if it's 0.

So essentially: the center is the cell adjacent (diagonally) to the colored cells toward the center. Each colored cell moves diagonally toward the center until one cell away, coloring that cell in its color.

Let me verify with the example. Colored cells: (2,9,1), (10,1,8), (10,9,2).
Row counts: row 2 has 1, row 10 has 2. So k = 10 (max count 2). cols_list = [1, 9]. a=1, b=9, c=5, d=4.
Candidates: r1 = 10-4 = 6, r2 = 10+4 = 14 (out of range, rows=12). So candidates = [6].
Check center (6,5): for (2,9): |2-6|=4, |9-5|=4. OK. (10,1): |10-6|=4, |1-5|=4 OK. (10,9): |10-6|=4, |9-5|=4 OK. Valid.
center = (6,5). Set grid[6][5]=5.
For each colored:
- (2,9,1): dr=-4, dc=4. s_dr=-1, s_dc=1. add=(5,6). grid[5][6]=1.
- (10,1,8): dr=4, dc=-4. s_dr=1, s_dc=-1. add=(7,4). grid[7][4]=8.
- (10,9,2): dr=4, dc=4. s_dr=1,s_dc=1. add=(7,6). grid[7][6]=2.
Output matches: row 5 col 6 = 1, row 6 col 5 = 5, row 7 col 4 = 8, row 7 col 6 = 2. Yes.

tools.name: show_example

input_grid.description: Rectangular matrix; each cell is an integer color 0–9.

output_grid.description: Rectangular matrix; each cell is an integer color 0–9.

tools.description: Show the Student a labeled input-output pair that you authored. If your output matches the rule, the pair is shown and you receive a success acknowledgement only. If it does not match, the pair is not shown and you receive the gold output so you can correct it.

tools.name: show_transformed_input

input_grid.description: Rectangular matrix; each cell is an integer color 0–9.

tools.description: Provide only an input grid. The environment applies the verifier and shows the resulting gold input-output pair to the student.

tools.name: query_student

input_grid.description: Rectangular matrix; each cell is an integer color 0–9.

tools.description: Probe the student with an input of your choice. You receive the student's predicted output, the gold output, and whether they matched. The student does not see the gold pair unless you later show it with show_example or show_transformed_input.

tools.name: start_exam
tools.description: End teaching and send the student to the exam: they must solve held-out generator inputs (unseen in demonstrations or probes) with the history so far. No further teaching after this.
